assistant:
At **20:00 on 6 January**, the grid’s only limit violation was **Bus_0–Bus_1 [L0]**, loaded to **114.4%** against the 100% limit. It had been within limits at **19:00**, but already close at **99.7%**.

The main factor was rising demand: demand near the line increased by **11.58 MW**, accounting for **47.0%** of the 14.8 percentage-point loading rise. That demand increase also remained the main cause when compared with a more comfortable afternoon point.

Two other factors contributed: output from the five units fell by **8.35 MW** (**33.8%** of the rise), and demand elsewhere increased by **5.19 MW** (**19.2%**). The study flagged abrupt output changes in the unit data—particularly for Gen_bus1, Gen_bus12 and Gen_bus4—so check those measurements before acting on that part of the explanation.

The line was outside its limit from **19:15**. These shares explain the change from the 19:00 reference; they do not mean any one factor alone caused the overload.
